Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 1. децембар ст. ст., „Свети Филарет Милостиви.“ — «Свети» is “saint” and not a rank, and «Милостиви» is the epithet “the Merciful” and not a grade, so it stays in the form. Section 6 wants the fullest form the calendar gives: the bare «Филарет» would have folded this man onto five other Philarets, and `foldchk.py` measured the fuller string on no folder at all.

saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 1ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιος Φιλάρετος ο Ελεήμων»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 1 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence on the page, and its heading dates him «(; - 792)». It is the same man, the almsgiver of Amnia in Paphlagonia whose granddaughter Maria married the emperor. Its Ἀπολυτίκιον and Κοντάκιον both name him and are taken here; the Μεγαλυνάριον it also prints is neither troparion nor kontakion and is not drafted. His skull, it says, is at the monastery of Agia Lavra of Kalavryta.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 14.12.2025 (1. децембар ст. ст.) — „Свети Филарет Милостиви.“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, and the second of two upgrades. The Romanian and Greek calendars already keep him on their own 1 December and the menologion scan found the folder. Quoted whole with its closing full stop (section 4); URL year 2025. `types` UNTOUCHED: «Милостиви» is “the Merciful”, an epithet and not a rank, and the folder’s `venerable` and `righteous` are what the other two books gave it; this book calls him «праведник» in the body, which is the `righteous` it already holds. `office` UNTOUCHED — none, and this book gives him none. `dates` REPLACED, for the same reason as the prophet above: the folder held `death` 792 off saint.gr’s heading «Άγιος Φιλάρετος ο Ελεήμων (; - 792)», and this book closes «Упокоји се овај праведник Божји 797. године». Five years apart, two books, nothing to choose between them: the interval is 792 to 797 and the note quotes both. Unlocated, so `map-span.test.mjs` is not in play. WHAT THE BOOK ADDS. The ox given to the ploughman and the horse given to the man called up with his horse to the war are already in the folder; the calf and the cow are not, nor is the detail that Maria was the daughter of his daughter Ипатија, nor the monastery of Родолфија where he lay down, nor the face shining like the sun, the fragrance after death and the wonders from the relics, nor the ninetieth-year blessing in which he foretold to each child how it would live out this age. FOUR PEOPLE NAMED AND NONE GETS A NEW ROW. Ирина the empress and her son Константин are already in the folder’s own prose from the other two books and are not saints the corpus holds; Марија the granddaughter and Теозва the wife likewise, both already in the prose. The forefather Јаков is named by this book as the comparison for the deathbed blessing AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT NAMED IN THE PARAGRAPH, because `related-floor.test.mjs` matches a display name in prose whether it is linked or not and a patriarch of Israel is not this man’s companion — the paragraph says “as the forefather of Israel once did to his sons” instead. No `locations`: Амнија, Paphlagonia and Родолфија are named and none is a coordinate the reader may set. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion. THE FOLD THIS FORM MAKES: none. `foldchk.py` measured «Филарет Милостиви» on no folder at all, and the bare «Филарет» — which six Philarets would have shared — was refused for exactly that reason: section 6 wants the fullest form the calendar gives, and the calendar gives the epithet.

death.note: Two books disagree and neither is chosen (CORPUS.md section 3). saint.gr’s heading reads «Άγιος Φιλάρετος ο Ελεήμων (; - 792)» and places his life «στους χρόνους του Κωνσταντίνου Πορφυρογέννητου και της μητρός αυτού Ειρήνης της Αττικής (780 - 797 μ.Χ.)»; the Охридски пролог for 1. децембар ст. ст. closes „Упокоји се овај праведник Божји 797. године.“

hymns.text: Θείας πίστεως περιουσίᾳ, διεσκόρπισας τοῖς δεομένοις τὸν προσιόντα σοι πλοῦτον, Φιλάρετε· καὶ εὐσπλαχνίᾳ κοσμήσας τὸν βίον σου, τὸν χορηγὸν τοῦ ἐλέους ἐδόξασας· Ὄν ἱκέτευε δοθῆναι τοῖς εὐφημοῦσι σε ῥανίδα οἰκτιρμῶν καὶ θεῖον ἔλεος.

source.text: saint.gr, Ἀπολυτίκιον, Ἤχος γ’, Θείας πίστεως — the first hymn on the page of «Άγιος Φιλάρετος ο Ελεήμων», and it names him and his almsgiving.

english.text: Out of the abundance of your divine faith you scattered among the needy the wealth that came to you, O Philaret; and adorning your life with compassion you glorified the giver of mercy. Entreat him to grant to those who praise you a drop of his pity and his divine mercy.

hymns.text: Τοῦ Ἰὼβ κτησάμενος, ἐν πειρασμοῖς τὴν ἀνδρείαν, τοῖς πτωχοῖς διένειμας, ὡς συμπαθὴς τὸν σὸν πλοῦτον· ὤφθης γάρ, τῆς εὐσπλαγχνίας ἔμψυχος βρύσις, νάμασι, τῶν θείων τρόπων σου ἱλαρύνων, τοὺς ἐκ πόθου σοι βοῶντας· χαῖροις θεράπον Χριστοῦ Φιλάρετε.

source.text: saint.gr, Κοντάκιον, Ἤχος γ’, Ἡ Παρθένος σήμερον — the kontakion on the page of «Άγιος Φιλάρετος ο Ελεήμων», and it names him and likens him to Job.

english.text: Having gained the manliness of Job in temptations, you dealt out your wealth to the poor as one who felt for them; for you were shown a living spring of compassion, gladdening with the streams of your divine ways those who cry to you with longing: rejoice, Philaret, servant of Christ.
